subject: History
note: The national curriculum in England, history programmes of study, key stage 2 (DfE 2013). Short headings; the gov.uk page has the full wording. The Tudors are taught as KS2.6.

sections.title: Key stage 2: what pupils should learn to do

points.text: changes in Britain from the Stone Age to the Iron Age
the Roman Empire and its impact on Britain
Britain's settlement by Anglo-Saxons and Scots
the Viking and Anglo-Saxon struggle for the Kingdom of England to the time of Edward the Confessor
a study of an aspect or theme in British history that extends pupils' chronological knowledge beyond 1066
the achievements of the earliest civilizations: Ancient Sumer, the Indus Valley, Ancient Egypt or the Shang Dynasty of Ancient China
Ancient Greece: Greek life and achievements and their influence on the western world
a non-European society that contrasts with British history: early Islamic civilization, Mayan civilization c. AD 900, or Benin (West Africa) c. AD 900-1300
a secure chronological knowledge of British, local and world history
connections, contrasts and trends over time; historical terms
historically valid questions about change, cause, similarity and difference, and significance
how knowledge of the past is built from a range of sources
